question.text: A short put at strike 83 with premium Rs. 0.075. At expiry USDINR is 82.50. What is the loss per unit?

explanation.text: The Logic: The short-put table on page 85 shows, at USDINR 82.50, premium received 0.075, payoff -0.500 and profit -0.425. Using the page 86 framework, max gain equals the premium received and BEP equals X - P, so the seller's per-unit P/L here is (83 - 82.50) - 0.075 = Rs. 0.425 loss. The Trap: The seller keeps the premium but must pay the intrinsic value to the buyer; reporting only the premium misses the larger payout the seller owes when the option is exercised against them. Note: Below the BEP of 82.925 the short-put seller's loss increases one-for-one with further declines in USDINR.
